title: Tally Ranges
statement: A cashier's tape lists daily net sales in values (which may be negative). Managers ask many questions of the form [left, right]: what is the total from day left through day right, inclusive? Return the answers to all queries, in order.

hints.content: Adding up each range directly costs up to n per query.
Many queries share work: they all add up stretches of the same tape.
Let prefix[i] be the total of the first i days, with prefix[0] = 0.
The total from left to right is prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left].
Build prefix once in O(n); then every query is O(1).

testCases.explanation: Whole range, middle and both ends.
Many long queries over a long tape.

solutions.title: Sum each range directly
solutions.intuition: Answer each question by adding the requested days.
solutions.approach: For each query, loop from left to right and add.
commonMistakes: Using i < right and missing the last day.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Direct summation is correct but repeats the same additions across overlapping queries.

solutions.title: Prefix sums
solutions.intuition: A range total is the difference of two running totals.
solutions.approach: Build prefix with prefix[0] = 0 and prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + values[i]. Answer each query with prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left].
solutions.pseudocode:
prefix[0] = 0; for i: prefix[i+1] = prefix[i] + values[i]
return [prefix[r+1] - prefix[l] for (l, r) in queries]
commonMistakes: Using prefix[right] - prefix[left], which drops the last day.
Forgetting the leading 0, which breaks queries that start at day 0.
solutions.interviewExplanation: I precompute running totals with a leading zero, so any inclusive range is prefix[r+1] - prefix[l]. That's O(n) preprocessing and O(1) per query. If the tape could change between queries I'd use a Fenwick tree for O(log n) updates and queries.
